text: {"frames":["A soft thud came from the library on the third floor, and the books had wandered off their shelves. Old Wiebe Paperhand pointed at a heap on the reading table, where {a} books lay in a pile. Across the room another heap held {b} books, and he wants each book back on its own shelf before the market bell rings. Which heap is bigger, or are the two heaps exactly the same?","A carrier pigeon flapped against the bakery door on the ground floor and dropped a letter meant for the tailor upstairs. The baker, Trijntje Klomp, read it and frowned. The tailor had ordered {a} bolts of blue cloth, but the cart that came up the canal carried only {b} bolts. Before she sends the bread van off, she needs to know whether the cloth is short, enough, or more than the tailor asked for.","The travelling theatre rolled into the courtyard just as the bell rang, but a row of wooden benches had gone missing in the night. Sientje-of-the-Dyke counted the benches that were left by the canal and found {a}. Her ticket book shows {b} guests who have paid for a seat tonight. Will there be enough seats for everyone, or will some guests have to stand by the windmill?","A sweet smell of warm cheese drifted down the stairs of the toy workshop, and a wind-up mouse came rattling out from under a crate. Its key was still turning, and it had dragged {a} cheese rounds into a dark corner. Joost Mallemolen counted the rounds left on the cheese maker's shelf, and there were {b} of them, all waiting for the market. Which pile holds more cheese, the mouse's corner or the shelf?","The fisher's nets are tangled again on the canal wall, and old Marit Netbrook calls up to you from her boat for help. She pulled {a} herring out of the left net and {b} herring out of the right net. Before she sells the catch at the stall by the lock, she wants to know which net gave her more fish."]}
